Basic = diluted per the FY2026 EPS note (potential ordinary shares antidilutive given the loss). Held FLAT: no material SBC to charge and no other dilutive instruments in the money.

inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The FULL IFRS-16 lease cash -- principal $8,042k PLUS interest $4,546k = $12,588k in FY2026 (6.05% of revenue), both from the FY2026 cash-flow statement -- is deducted inside the flow build as `lease_cost_pct_path` (modelled as a $12.6m premises bill escalating 2%/yr, so it rises as a share of revenue in the bear case and falls in the bull case), and lease liabilities ($69,532k) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. net_debt = interest-bearing liabilities $35,241k less cash $8,266k = $26,975k, which ties to the company's own 'Net debt at 31 March'. The 2026-08-20 build deducted the principal only (3.9% of revenue) while describing itself as principal + interest; that alone overstated every projected year's owner FCF by ~$4.5-5m on flows of $2-15m.
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-denominated flows discounted at a NZD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.5% (NZ 10yr govt, mid-2026), ERP 5.5%, beta 1.15 (cyclical building-materials processor) => unlevered CoE proxy ~10.8%. A +3.0pp small-cap/illiquidity/control premium is stacked on top (base WACC 13.5%) for: (i) micro-cap NZX/ASX dual-listed stock with market cap ~NZ$23m and thin free float (2,205 NZX holders, largest non-Amari holder <0.3%), (ii) 51% single-shareholder control (Amari/MGI) via board representation, (iii) only ~11 months since the Sept-2025 recapitalisation removed going-concern doubt -- covenant headroom is still unproven through a full cycle. This mirrors the stacked-WACC treatment applied to comparable NZX micro-caps in this folder (2CC.NZ 19%, CDI.NZ / AGL.NZ 17%). Per section 7(f), construction-cycle risk itself is charged in the flows via the probability-weighted scenarios, NOT via a further WACC premium or per-scenario WACC spread beyond the small bear/bull adjustment used to reflect distinct capital-structure/solvency risk in the bear case (15.0%) versus a lower-risk bull case (12.5%) -- this spread reflects solvency-tail risk in the bear case specifically (covenant stress), not cyclicality generally, which lives in the bear case's lower growth/margin path.
inputs.model: Owner-FCF DCF (operating company, non-US/cyclical adaptations per dcf-methods skill section 7); rebuilt 2026-09-15
inputs.notes: MPG.NZ is an operating industrial company (glass processing/glazing, NZ + AU construction) -- owner-FCF DCF, not a REIT/bank/LIC model. Section 7 adaptations: (a) NZD-built WACC; (b) lease treatment B (full lease cash in the flows, lease liabilities out of net debt); (c) no NCI; (d) no non-operating assets to strip; (e) SBC-zero market, SBC rows explicit at 0%, band_position null. The flow formula is the dashboard component engine's: EBIT = revenue x (EBITDA margin - SBC% - lease% - D&A%); cash tax on max(0, EBIT); FCF = EBIT - tax + D&A - capex + wc_capture x (revenue change), with wc_capture NEGATIVE (-14%) because net working capital (receivables + inventory + other current assets - payables - deferred income = $29,318k, 14.1% of revenue) is an investment that grows with sales, not a prepaid-subscription inflow. D&A% is ex right-of-use depreciation (3.5% vs 3.9% actual) so EBIT does not charge the lease twice. 10-year explicit horizon: margin is still recovering off a cyclical trough at year 5. REBUILT 2026-09-15 -- see rebuild_log.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2026 underlying owner FCF on the EV basis, NZD thousands: OCF 15,675 + bank interest paid 4,010 - working-capital release 8,194 - capex 2,849 - lease principal 8,042 - interest income 49 = 551. The component route gives 2,726 before the 2,102 of restructuring cash (EBITDA before significant items 18,241 - lease cash 12,588 - capex 2,849 - cash tax 78). The reported FCF of 12,826 (OCF - capex) is 64% a one-off payables/inventory release (cash-flow reconciliation p.14) and includes neither lease principal nor the flattering of OCF by bank interest being an equity, not an EV, charge.
inputs.tax_losses_note: Recognised deferred tax asset on tax losses $7,319k (~$26m of losses at 28%); the Sept-2025 raise breached shareholder continuity (imputation credits wiped, note 6.1), so the shield is treated as finite: cash tax ramps 0% -> 28% statutory from FY2030 to FY2034.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (equity CAGR rejected as the primary driver -- see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.8% to -7.4%) and revenue CAGR (-2.2% to -7.6%) both negative but NEITHER is usable as a forward growth proxy without adjustment. FY2026 shareholders' equity ($59,958k) was inflated by the Sept-2025 $23.9m dilutive capital raise, not organic compounding -- ex-raise equity would have kept falling toward the FY2025 trough ($35,582k). EPS CAGR is not computable: FY2026 EPS (-6.0c) sits on a weighted-average share count blended across the 40:1 consolidation and is not comparable to any prior year's EPS on a pre-consolidation basis. Owner FCF CAGR is not computable either -- FY2025 owner FCF was negative (-$8,525k after lease-principal and interest-income deductions) so no valid CAGR base exists between FY2025 and FY2026. None of the standard CAGR anchors are usable here; the DCF growth path is instead built bottom-up from FY2026 actuals, management's explicit FY2027 'no substantive market growth' guidance, and the $4m realised cost-out program, per the component-build method (section 2 of owner-fcf.md).
historical_growth.fcf_note: Owner FCF (EV basis, ex working-capital swings) FY2025 approx -8.5m, FY2026 +0.6m; no CAGR is definable. Pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin (EBITDA before significant items less full lease cash) ran 12.3% FY2021, 6.1% FY2022, 7.2% FY2023, 5.4% FY2024, 2.1% FY2025, 2.7% FY2026 -- the base case's 11% post-IFRS-16 mid-cycle margin is ~5% on this basis, i.e. an FY2023-24 level, not a return to FY2018-21.

base.narrative: Base case: FY27 essentially flat (management's 'no substantive market growth' guidance) as the $4m FY26 cost-out delivers its full-year benefit; EBITDA margin (before significant items, post-IFRS-16) recovers from 8.76% toward 11% -- about 5% after the $12.6m premises bill, an FY2023-24 level and well below the FY2018/FY2021 peaks -- reflecting the Commerce Commission's finding that NZ glass processing remains structurally oversupplied. Modest volume recovery from FY28 as NZ/AU consents stabilise and Building Code / NatHERS lift the double-glazing mix. Cash tax shielded by the recognised tax losses until FY2030, then ramps to the 28% statutory rate. Owner FCF builds from ~$0.6m (FY26 underlying) to ~$2.7m FY27 and ~$5m by FY31: this is a business that earns roughly its cost of capital on an ex-lease EV of ~$47m, so most of the equity value sits in the bull case, not the base.
base.terminal_cap_basis: 14.9x year-10 owner FCF = 5.5x year-10 pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA (14325k), the stock's own normal-year EV/EBITDA ceiling; binds only if Gordon at WACC/g exceeds it

bull.narrative: Bull case: the failed Viridian takeover and persistent NZ oversupply keep consolidation optionality alive -- a rationalisation of processing capacity (Metro or a competitor exiting) restores pricing power faster than base assumes; AGG's import-model transition stabilises early and Australia's 1.2-million-homes target flows into volumes; Building Code / NatHERS drive mix-shift to Low-E / laminated / frameless product. Margin reaches 13.5% post-IFRS-16 (about 8% pre-IFRS-16, an FY2023 level, still short of FY2021's 12%). Terminal value is capped at 5.5x pre-IFRS-16 EV/EBITDA, the upper-middle of the stock's own normal-year trading range, so no re-rating beyond history is assumed even here. Amari (51%) or a strategic buying the minority at a premium is the realistic exit path.
bull.terminal_cap_basis: 11.0x year-10 owner FCF = 5.5x year-10 pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA (28472k), the stock's own normal-year EV/EBITDA ceiling; binds only if Gordon at WACC/g exceeds it

bear.narrative: Bear case: the construction downturn deepens rather than stabilises -- NZ consent momentum turns into a further multi-year decline and Victoria stays subdued longer than AGG's cost base can absorb. The premises bill ($12.6m, escalating) is fixed while revenue falls, so the pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin sits near 1-2% and owner FCF is negative for the first three years; the equity is worth less than zero against $27m of bank debt (the covenant path -- renegotiated Sept-2025, facility to Sept-2028 -- is the binding constraint, not the model). WACC 15.0% carries a solvency-tail premium specific to this path. Terminal cap 5.5x pre-IFRS-16 EV/EBITDA (does not bind: Gordon at 15%/1.5% is lower).
bear.terminal_cap_basis: 20.0x year-10 owner FCF = 5.5x year-10 pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA (3611k), the stock's own normal-year EV/EBITDA ceiling; binds only if Gordon at WACC/g exceeds it

no_re_rate_reference.description: Memo: terminal value at the MEDIAN normal-year pre-IFRS-16 EV/EBITDA (5.15x) instead of Gordon, base-case flows. The gap to the house value is the price of the exit-multiple assumption.
no_re_rate_reference.note: Above the house base IV because Gordon at a 13.5% WACC capitalises year-10 FCF at only ~3.3x EBITDA; the market's own history is the more generous of the two.

entry_price.method: Sum of interim FCF at 15% + terminal value rebuilt AT the 15% hurdle (min of Gordon at 15%/g and the same FCF-multiple cap) discounted 10 years, less net debt, per share; all three scenarios, probability-weighted.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate; the 13.5% row equals the base IV and the 15% row the base entry price.

sensitivity.note: Base-case flows held fixed; only the Gordon terminal value moves. The FCF-multiple cap (14.9x, = 5.5x pre-IFRS-16 EV/EBITDA) binds in the low-WACC / high-growth corner, which is why those cells flatten. Values in NZD per share against a $0.83 price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% house default): only a year past a dilutive recapitalisation, management withholding FY27 numeric guidance, and a fixed $12.6m premises bill that turns any further revenue decline straight into negative owner FCF. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): needs NZ capacity rationalisation, AU volume recovery and margin execution beyond the actioned cost-out to line up. Base 50%. Note the bear IV is NEGATIVE (equity worth less than the bank debt on those flows) and the base IV sits near the tick floor, so the weighted value is carried almost entirely by the bull case -- the honest description of a controlled, asset-heavy turnaround trading at 0.34x book.

sanity_check.methodology: Step 8c on a LEASE-CONSISTENT basis. MPG adopted IFRS 16 in FY2020, so from FY2021 reported EBITDA excludes ~$9-12.6m/yr of premises rent while lease liabilities ($69.5m at FY2026, more than the bank debt) sit outside 'net debt'. Comparing an ex-lease EV with a post-IFRS-16 EBITDA -- what the 2026-08-20 build and scripts/sanity_check.py both do -- reads FY2021-26 multiples ~2-3x too low against the pre-IFRS-16 FY2018-19 years and calls the stock 'cheap at 2.7x'. Two consistent lenses are used instead: (i) ex-lease EV / (EBITDA before significant items - full lease cash) = pre-IFRS-16 EV/EBITDA, comparable with FY2018-19; (ii) lease-inclusive EV / post-IFRS-16 EBITDA for FY2022-26 where lease liabilities are stored. FY-end prices are raw Yahoo monthly closes x 185.378m pre-consolidation shares; FY2026 is the post-consolidation $1.00 x 24.591m. Note scripts/sanity_check.py will keep reporting the inconsistent basis for this ticker.
sanity_check.price_series_check: Yahoo's raw monthly series is NOT consolidation-adjusted: $0.040 (2026-01) jumps to $1.055 (2026-02) across the 40:1 consolidation of 6-Mar-2026 (the Feb bar already carries the post-consolidation quote). The rights issue + Amari placement (Sept-2025) took 185.4m shares to 983.6m, then 40:1 to 24.6m; the $23.9m was raised at $0.03 = $1.20 post-consolidation, so the current $0.83 (2026-09-15, live NZX regular close) is 31% below the recapitalisation price. Market cap $20.4m; ex-lease EV $47.4m.

historical_multiple_range.basis: ex-lease EV / pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA before significant items (lens i)
historical_multiple_range.normal_year_range: 3.7x (FY2021) to 6.6x (FY2022); FY2025 15.8x and FY2026 9.1x are trough-earnings outliers

sanity_check.outcome: PASS. Base-case terminal value is 3.44x year-10 pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA (Gordon at 13.5%/2.5%), inside the 3.7-6.6x normal-year range; the bull terminal is capped at 5.5x. The market itself is at 8.4x trough pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA / 6.4x lease-inclusive -- NOT the 2.7x the prior build reported -- and 0.34x book. The prior build's base IV of $2.50 implied 8.7x lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA and 15.7x pre-IFRS-16, above anything the stock has traded at in a decade.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Rebuilt 2026-09-15: (1) lease cost = principal + interest ($12,588k, 6.05% of revenue) instead of principal only; (2) working capital an outflow on growth (-14% of revenue change) instead of a +12% inflow; (3) cash tax on max(0, EBIT) with EBIT ex right-of-use depreciation, instead of a credit on a negative EBIT that charged the lease twice; (4) sanity multiples recomputed on a lease-consistent basis and the terminal cap re-expressed as 5.5x pre-IFRS-16 EV/EBITDA. Base IV $2.50 -> see valuation.base; weighted IV $2.87 -> see probability_weighted.

valuation_philosophy: The 2026-08-20 build reported +205% base-case upside. Almost all of it was mechanical: the lease line deducted only the $8.0m principal and not the $4.5m of lease interest (while the text said principal + interest), working capital was booked as a cash inflow on growth for a manufacturer that carries 14% of revenue in receivables and inventory, and cash tax came through as a credit on a negative EBIT. Together those added ~$5-7m a year to flows that are really $2-5m, and the 'conservative' 6x-FCF terminal cap, calibrated against an EV/EBITDA history that mixed pre- and post-IFRS-16 years, actually implied ~8.7x lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA against a stock that has never traded above 6.6x on a like-for-like basis. Rebuilt on the dashboard's own component formula, the business earns roughly its cost of capital on an ex-lease EV of ~$47m: the base case is worth about the current price, the bear case is negative, and the equity value lives in the bull case (capacity rationalisation or a control transaction by Amari, the 51% holder). At $0.83 the market pays 0.34x book / 60% of NTA ($1.38/share) for that option. A reader who believes the assets (two NZ plants, three AU sites, $35m of PP&E) will be monetised near book should look at the bull case; one who believes NZ oversupply is structural should look at the bear.
